claim: The cryo-EM structure of a six-protein core COMPASS subcomplex bound to a ubiquitinated nucleosome was determined at 3.37 Å resolution.
source: We report here the cryo-EM structure of a six-protein core COMPASS subcomplex, which can methylate H3K4 and be stimulated by H2B-Ub, bound to a ubiquitinated nucleosome.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the structure was determined and the resolution is provided in the Results section and Table 1.

claim: COMPASS spans the face of the nucleosome, recognizing ubiquitin on one face and methylating H3 on the opposing face.
source: Our structure shows that COMPASS spans the face of the nucleosome, recognizing ubiquitin on one face of the nucleosome and methylating H3 on the opposing face.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data showing distances between H3 exit points and the Set1 active site.

claim: Methylation of histone H3K4 is a hallmark of actively transcribed genes.
source: Methylation of histone H3K4 is a hallmark of actively transcribed genes that depends on mono-ubiquitination of histone H2B (H2B-Ub).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by multiple citations in the introduction.

claim: H3K4 methylation depends on mono-ubiquitination of histone H2B at Lysine 120 (Lys 123 in yeast).
source: Methylation of nucleosomal H3K4 depends on the prior ubiquitination of histone H2B (H2B-Ub) at Lysine 120 (Lys 123 in yeast) (Dover et al., 2002; Shahbazian et al., 2005; Sun and Allis, 2002)
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations from prior literature.

claim: Set1 is the methyltransferase subunit of COMPASS that catalyzes H3K4 methylation in yeast.
source: H3K4 methylation in yeast is catalyzed by Set1, the methyltransferase subunit of COMPASS.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The Set1 RxxxRR motif adopts a helix that mediates bridging contacts between the nucleosome, ubiquitin and COMPASS.
source: The critical Set1 RxxxRR motif adopts a helix that mediates bridging contacts between the nucleosome, ubiquitin and COMPASS.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data in Figure 4.

claim: Set1 undergoes multiple structural rearrangements to cement interactions with the nucleosome and with ubiquitin.
source: As compared to the structure of the isolated core complex, Set1 undergoes multiple structural rearrangements to cement interactions with the nucleosome and with ubiquitin.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and demonstrated by structural comparisons in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: H3K4 is methylated in humans by the six related SET1/MLL family of methyltransferases.
source: H3K4 is methylated in yeast by the Set1 methyltransferase (Roguev et al., 2001), which can attach up to three methyl groups to the lysine ε-amino group (Santos-Rosa et al., 2002), and in humans by the six related SET1/MLL family of methyltransferases (Meeks and Shilatifard, 2017).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citation.

claim: H2B-Ub and H3K4 di- and tri-methylation are strongly associated with active transcription in both yeast and humans.
source: H2B-Ub and H3K4 di- and tri-methylation are strongly associated with active transcription in both yeast and humans (Barski et al., 2007; Jung et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2005; Minsky et al., 2008; Pokholok et al., 2005; Santos-Rosa et al., 2002; Shieh et al., 2011; Steger et al., 2008).
evidence: Explicitly stated with multiple supporting citations.

claim: COMPASS contains Sgh1 (Cps15), Sdc1 (Cps25), Swd3 (Cps30), Swd2 (Cps35), Spp1 (Cps40), Swd1 (Cps50), Bre2 (Cps60), and Set1.
source: In yeast, H3K4 is methylated by the evolutionarily conserved COMplex of Proteins ASsociated with Set1 (COMPASS) (Miller et al., 2001; Shilatifard, 2012), which contains Sgh1 (Cps15), Sdc1 (Cps25), Swd3 (Cps30), Swd2 (Cps35), Spp1 (Cps40), Swd1 (Cps50), Bre2 (Cps60), as well as Set1 (Miller et al., 2001; Nagy et al., 2002; Roguev et al., 2001; Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: Set1 is inactive on its own.
source: Set1, which contains a conserved SET methyltransferase domain, is inactive on its own (Avdic et al., 2011; Dou et al., 2006; Patel et al., 2009; Southall et al., 2009).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: A core subcomplex comprising Sdc1, Swd3, Swd1, Bre2 and Set1 constitutes the minimal set of subunits required to support full Set1 methyltransferase activity.
source: Multiple studies have identified a core subcomplex comprising Sdc1, Swd3, Swd1, Bre2 and Set1 which constitutes the minimal set of subunits required to support full Set1 methyltransferase activity (Dou et al., 2006; Patel et al., 2009; Schneider et al., 2005; Southall et al., 2009).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: The core subcomplex of COMPASS is highly conserved across all eukaryotes, with human WDR5/RbBP5/ASH2L/DPY30 corresponding to yeast Swd3/Swd1/Bre2/Sdc1.
source: This core subcomplex of COMPASS is highly conserved across all eukaryotes, with human WDR5/RbBP5/ASH2L/DPY30 corresponding to yeast Swd3/Swd1/Bre2/Sdc1 (Miller et al., 2001; Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: The ability of COMPASS activity to be fully stimulated on nucleosomes by H2B ubiquitination depends upon the presence of Spp1 and the RxxxRR motif in the N-set region of Set1.
source: The ability of COMPASS activity to be fully stimulated on nucleosomes by H2B ubiquitination depends upon the presence of an additional COMPASS subunit, Spp1, as well as the RxxxRR motif in the N-set region of Set1 which is also referred to as the Arginine Rich Motif (ARM) (Hsu et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: COMPASS adopts a Y-shaped, highly intertwined structure with the Set1 catalytic domain at its core.
source: Structural studies of the yeast core subcomplex (Hsu et al., 2018) and the H2B-ubiquitin-sensing subcomplex (Qu et al., 2018; Takahashi et al., 2011) have shown that COMPASS adopts a Y-shaped, highly intertwined structure with the Set1 catalytic domain at its core.
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: A recent structure of the human MLL1 core complex bound to a ubiquitinated nucleosome revealed the underlying mechanisms of nucleosome recognition by human COMPASS-like complexes.
source: Furthermore, a recent structure of the related human MLL1 core complex bound to a ubiquitinated nucleosome revealed the underlying mechanisms of nucleosome recognition by human COMPASS-like complexes (Xue et al., 2019).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citation.

claim: A recent structure of the COMPASS complex from K. Lactis has shown how COMPASS binds to a ubiquitinated nucleosome.
source: In addition, a recent structure of the related COMPASS complex from K. Lactis has shown how COMPASS binds to a ubiquitinated nucleosome (Hsu et al., 2019).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citation.

claim: COMPASS methylates H3K4 in an asymmetric manner by targeting H2B-Ub and H3K4 on opposite sides of the nucleosome.
source: The position of the Set1 catalytic domain suggests that COMPASS methylates H3K4 in an asymmetric manner by targeting H2B-Ub and H3K4 on opposite sides of the nucleosome.
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by structural data showing distances in Figure 1d.

claim: The RxxxRR helix forms the bottom edge of an extended ubiquitin interaction crevice that underlies the structural basis of H2B-ubiquitin recognition by COMPASS.
source: Structuring of a critical RxxxRR motif to form a helix enables the complex to associate with the nucleosome acidic patch, with the RxxxRR helix forming the bottom edge of an extended ubiquitin interaction crevice that underlies the structural basis of H2B-ubiquitin recognition by COMPASS.
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by structural data in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Interactions with the H2B-linked ubiquitin are highly plastic among different ubiquitin-activated methyltransferases.
source: Comparison with other ubiquitin-activated methyltransferases shows that interactions with the H2B-linked ubiquitin are highly plastic and suggests how a single ubiquitin mark can be utilized by several different enzymes.
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by structural comparisons in Figure 5.

claim: The structure provides the first example of trans-nucleosome histone crosstalk.
source: Our findings shed light on the long-standing mystery of how H2B-Ub is recognized by COMPASS and provide the first example of trans-nucleosome histone crosstalk.
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by structural data showing asymmetric recognition.

claim: Lysine-to-norleucine mutations greatly increase the affinity of SET-domain methyltransferases for their substrates in a SAM-dependent manner.
source: Lysine-to-norleucine mutations have been shown to greatly increase the affinity of SET-domain methyltransferases for their substrates in a S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent manner (Jayaram et al., 2016; Lewis et al., 2013; Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Explicitly stated with supporting citations.

claim: COMPASS binds to unmodified and H2B-Ub nucleosomes with the same apparent affinity.
source: Surprisingly, COMPASS binds to unmodified and H2B-Ub nucleosomes with the same apparent affinity, indicating that H2B-Ub does not contribute significantly to the energy of COMPASS binding to the nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by gel mobility shift assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: H2B-Ub nucleosomes containing the H3K4Nle mutation bind COMPASS with 2–5 fold higher affinity than unmodified nucleosomes.
source: However, H2B-Ub nucleosomes that also contain the H3K4Nle mutant bind COMPASS with 2–5 fold higher affinity than unmodified nucleosomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, compare the 0.125 µM lane for all samples).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by gel mobility shift assay data.

claim: Two COMPASS complexes are bound to opposite faces of the nucleosome in a pseudo-symmetric 2:1 arrangement in the reconstruction.
source: In the reconstruction, two COMPASS complexes are bound to opposite faces of the nucleosome in a pseudo-symmetric 2:1 arrangement (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Only one of the two bound COMPASS assemblies resolved to high resolution.
source: However, only one of the two bound COMPASS assemblies resolved to high resolution.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Compared to isolated S. cerevisiae COMPASS, nucleosome-bound COMPASS flexes around the central Set1 catalytic domain and moves Swd3, Spp1 and Swd1 toward the nucleosome by ~36 Å.
source: Compared to isolated S. cerevisiae COMPASS (Qu et al., 2018), nucleosome-bound COMPASS flexes around the central Set1 catalytic domain and moves Swd3, Spp1 and Swd1 toward the nucleosome by ~36 Å (Figure 1c).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The Set1 active site is oriented away from the nucleosome and contains density for the SAM cofactor and the bound H3 tail.
source: The Set1 active site is oriented away from the nucleosome and contains density for the SAM cofactor and the bound H3 tail (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The intervening sequence of the H3 tail from its exit point in the nucleosome (P38) to the first resolved residue in the Set1 active site (R8) is not visible in the maps, suggesting that these residues are highly mobile.
source: The intervening sequence of the H3 tail, from its exit point in the nucleosome (P38) to the first resolved residue in the Set1 active site (R8), is not visible in the maps, suggesting that these residues are highly mobile (Figure 1b,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1b,d.

claim: The Set1 active site is positioned much closer to the exit point of the trans-H3 subunit (~35 Å) than to the exit point of the cis-H3 subunit (~88 Å).
source: The Set1 active site is positioned much closer to the exit point of the H3 subunit on the opposite face of the nucleosome (trans-H3,~35 Å) than to the exit point of the H3 subunit on the same side of the nucleosome (cis-H3,~88 Å, Figure 1d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1d.

claim: COMPASS methylates the nucleosome in an asymmetric manner by recognizing ubiquitin on one face of the nucleosome and targeting H3K4 on the opposite, trans-H3, face of the nucleosome.
source: This arrangement therefore indicates that COMPASS methylates the nucleosome in an asymmetric manner by recognizing ubiquitin on one face of the nucleosome and targeting H3K4 on the opposite, trans-H3, face of the nucleosome.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by distance measurements in Figure 1d.

claim: A pair of loops in Swd1 anchor COMPASS near the C-terminal H2B helix.
source: A pair of loops in Swd1 anchor COMPASS near the C-terminal H2B helix (Figure 3).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: A long helix in Set1 containing the RxxxRR motif extends along the surface of the histone core and makes multiple interactions with the nucleosome acidic patch formed by histones H2A and H2B.
source: In addition, a long helix in Set1 containing the RxxxRR motif (Kim et al., 2013) extends along the surface of the histone core and makes multiple interactions with the nucleosome acidic patch formed by histones H2A and H2B (Figure 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Set1, Bre2 and Swd1 bind to the H2B-linked ubiquitin, providing a structural basis for the crosstalk between H2B-Ubiquitination and H3K4 methylation.
source: Finally, Set1, Bre2 and Swd1 bind to the H2B-linked ubiquitin (Figures 5 and 6), providing a structural basis for the crosstalk between H2B-Ubiquitination and H3K4 methylation.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: COMPASS interacts with DNA in three distinct locations, thereby orienting the complex on the face of the nucleosome.
source: COMPASS interacts with DNA in three distinct locations, thereby orienting the complex on the face of the nucleosome (Figure 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The nucleosomal DNA docks into a concave surface at the interface of Bre2 and Set1.
source: At one end of COMPASS, the nucleosomal DNA docks into a concave surface at the interface of Bre2 and Set1 (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2a,b.

claim: Bre2 K318 is in a position to interact directly with the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA.
source: In particular, Bre2 K318 is in a position to interact directly with the sugar-phosphate backbone (Figure 2b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: COMPASS contacts the DNA at two distinct interfaces mediated by Spp1 and Swd1 on the opposing edge of the nucleosome.
source: On the opposing edge of the nucleosome, COMPASS contacts the DNA at two distinct interfaces mediated by Spp1 and Swd1 (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: A loop in Spp1 (residues 241–261) contains a patch of positively-charged amino acids (KRKKKK) that likely interact with the negatively charged DNA backbone and major groove.
source: This Spp1 loop (Figure 2c) contains a patch of positively-charged amino acids (KRKKKK) that likely interact with the negatively charged DNA backbone and major groove.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Swd1 interacts with the nucleosomal DNA using two highly conserved basic residues, R236 and K266, which emanate from loops in blade 5 of the Swd1 WD40 domain.
source: Swd1 interacts with the nucleosomal DNA using two highly conserved basic resides, R236 and K266, which emanate from loops in blade 5 of the Swd1 WD40 domain (Figure 2d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Substitution of Swd1 K266 with an alanine decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation in yeast.
source: Substitution of Swd1 K266 with an alanine decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation in yeast (Figure 3c–d), indicating that the loss of even a single DNA contact can impair COMPASS function.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3c-d.

claim: Similar interactions between COMPASS subunits (Bre2, Spp1 and Swd1) and nucleosomal DNA have been observed in the human MLL1 complex and the K. lactis COMPASS complex.
source: Importantly, similar interactions between these COMPASS subunits (Bre2, Spp1 and Swd1) and nucleosomal DNA have recently been observed in the human MLL1 complex (Xue et al., 2019) and the K. lactis COMPASS complex (Hsu et al., 2019), indicating that these DNA interactions are critical for COMPASS function and are highly conserved.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Swd1 contains two loops that interact with three different histones in the nucleosome core.
source: The structure reveals that Swd1 contains two loops that interact with three different histones in the nucleosome core (Figure 3a).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Swd1 Loop 1 connects β21 and β22, and, along with the edge of β-strand 25, embraces the H2B C-terminal helix, ɑ4.
source: Swd1 Loop 1 connects β21 and β22, and, along with the edge of β-strand 25, embraces the H2B C-terminal helix, ɑ4 (Figure 3a).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: At the tip of Loop 1, Swd1 V263 and I264 insert into a small hydrophobic crevice at the three-helix interface consisting of H2B helices, ɑ3 and ɑ4, and H2A ɑ3.
source: At the tip of L, V263 and I264 insert into a small hydrophobic crevice at the three-helix interface consisting of H2B helices, ɑ3 and ɑ4, and H2A ɑ3 (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a,b.

claim: The Swd1 I264A mutation completely abolished H3K4 di- and tri-methylation and greatly reduced H3K4 mono-methylation.
source: As shown in Figure 3c, the substitution with the greatest effect was Swd1 I264A, which completely abolished H3K4 di- and tri-methylation and greatly reduced H3K4 mono-methylation (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3c,d.

claim: The interaction between Swd1 Loop 1 and the H2A/H2B hydrophobic crevice is critical for COMPASS activity.
source: I264 is positioned in the center of the H2A/H2B hydrophobic crevice and the strong defect in H3K4 methylation seen for the I264A mutation indicates that this interaction is critical for COMPASS activity in vivo.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by mutagenesis data in Figure 3c,d.

claim: Loop 1 is highly conserved and the residues that correspond to V263 and I264 are always hydrophobic in character.
source: Loop 1 is highly conserved (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and the residues that correspond to V263 and I264 are always hydrophobic in character, indicating that that the interaction we observe between Loop 1 and the histone octamer is structurally conserved among Swd1 homologs.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The human MLL1 core complex subunit, Rbbp5, binds to the histone octamer using a similar interface to Swd1.
source: Indeed, the human MLL1 core complex subunit, Rbbp5, binds to the histone octamer using a similar interface (Xue et al., 2019) and another recent study reports that the K. lactis COMPASS complex Swd1 subunit also utilizes the hydrophobic cleft interface in a similar manner (Hsu et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Swd1 Loop 2 connects β-strands β23 and β24 and is oriented toward the histone H3 ɑ2-ɑ3 loop and histone H4 ɑ3.
source: In addition to Swd1 L, Loop 2 connects β-strands β23 and β24 and is oriented toward the histone H3 ɑ2-ɑ3 loop and histone H4 ɑ3 (Figure 3b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3b.

claim: At the tip of Loop 2, Swd1 S289 forms a hydrogen bond with H3 K79.
source: At the tip of Loop 2, S289 forms a hydrogen bond with H3 K79.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Loop 2 is not well conserved and the contact it makes with H3K79 is not recapitulated in other COMPASS-like complexes.
source: As compared to L, Loop 2 is not well conserved (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and the contact it makes with H3K79 is not recapitulated in other COMPASS-like complexes (Xue et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The interaction between Swd1 and the nucleosome is conserved from yeast to humans and is critical for COMPASS function in vivo.
source: Taken together, these results show that the interaction between Swd1 and the nucleosome is conserved from yeast to humans and is critical for COMPASS function in vivo.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by structural and mutagenesis data.

claim: The RxxxRR motif in the N-set region of Set1 is critical for stimulation of methyltransferase activity by H2B ubiquitination.
source: The arginine-rich RxxxRR motif in the N-set region of Set1 is critical for stimulation of methyltransferase activity by H2B ubiquitination and mutants in this motif impair COMPASS activity in yeast (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: In isolated yeast COMPASS, the RxxxRR motif is disordered.
source: In isolated yeast COMPASS (Qu et al., 2018), the RxxxRR motif is disordered.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: When bound to the H2B-Ub nucleosome, Set1 residues 897–921 become ordered, forming a long helix that passes underneath COMPASS and makes extensive contacts with the nucleosome acidic patch.
source: When bound to the H2B-Ub nucleosome, Set1 residues 897–921 become ordered, forming a long helix that passes underneath COMPASS and makes extensive contacts with the nucleosome acidic patch (Figure 4a–e), as well as with the H2B-linked ubiquitin (see below).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4a-e.

claim: The RxxxRR helix docks on the nucleosome surface parallel to the C-terminal helix ɑ4 of histone H2B, positioning multiple arginine residues opposite the negatively charged residues of H2A that make up the acidic patch.
source: The RxxxRR helix docks on the nucleosome surface parallel to the C-terminal helix ɑ4 of histone H2B, positioning multiple arginine residues opposite the negatively charged residues of H2A that make up the acidic patch (Figure 4d,e and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4d,e and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Set1 R908 is in a position to contact H2A residue E56 and H2B E113.
source: Residues in the Set1 RxxxRR helix form several specific electrostatic interactions with acidic patch residues: R908 is in a position to contact H2A residue E56 and H2B E113, R904 contacts H2A residue E61 and E64 and R901 contacts H2A residues D90 and E92 (Figure 4d,e).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4d,e.

claim: Set1 R904 contacts H2A residue E61 and E64.
source: Residues in the Set1 RxxxRR helix form several specific electrostatic interactions with acidic patch residues: R908 is in a position to contact H2A residue E56 and H2B E113, R904 contacts H2A residue E61 and E64 and R901 contacts H2A residues D90 and E92 (Figure 4d,e).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4d,e.

claim: Set1 R901 contacts H2A residues D90 and E92.
source: Residues in the Set1 RxxxRR helix form several specific electrostatic interactions with acidic patch residues: R908 is in a position to contact H2A residue E56 and H2B E113, R904 contacts H2A residue E61 and E64 and R901 contacts H2A residues D90 and E92 (Figure 4d,e).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4d,e.

claim: The extensive electrostatic network mediated by the RxxxRR helix is flanked by interactions between Set1 R936 and H2A D72 on one side and between R909 and H2B S112 on the other.
source: The extensive electrostatic network mediated by the RxxxRR helix is flanked by interactions between Set1 R936 and H2A D72 on one side and between R909 and H2B S112 on the other.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The RxxxRR motif is conserved in human Set1 orthologs, but not in the human paralogs MLL1-4.
source: Interestingly, the RxxxRR motif is conserved in human Set1 orthologs, but not in the human paralogs MLL1-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) which have recently been shown not to bind the nucleosome acidic patch (Xue et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nucleosome binding is accompanied by a profound restructuring of Set1 ɑ-helix, 926–933, which unravels and forms an extended strand that lies parallel to the RxxxRR helix.
source: In addition to formation of the RxxxRR helix, nucleosome binding is accompanied by a profound restructuring of Set1 ɑ-helix, 926–933, which unravels and forms an extended strand that lies parallel to the RxxxRR helix (Figure 4f and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4f and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: A combined R909, R908 and R904 triple mutant abolished COMPASS activity in vitro and in vivo.
source: Previous mutagenesis studies of the N-set region of yeast Set1 (Kim et al., 2013) showed that a combined R909, R908 and R904 triple mutant abolished COMPASS activity in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: Set1 R936A and R936E mutations both reduced H3K4 methylation.
source: As compared to wild-type, R936A and R936E Set1 mutations both reduced H3K4 methylation (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4g,h.

claim: The charge reversal mutation, Set1 R936E, almost entirely abolished di- and tri-methylation by COMPASS.
source: The charge reversal mutation, R936E, was more severe and almost entirely abolished di- and tri-methylation by COMPASS (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4g,h.

claim: Individual alanine substitutions of Set1 R901A, R904A and R908A reduced mono-methylation by COMPASS and abolished di-, and tri-methylation.
source: Individual alanine substitutions of R901A, R904A and R901A reduced mono-methylation by COMPASS and abolished di-, and tri-methylation.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The Set1 R909A mutation greatly reduced di-and tri-methylation.
source: The R909A mutation, which does not form electrostatic contacts with the acidic patch, greatly reduced di-and tri-methylation.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The Set1 quadruple mutant R901A, R904A, R908A and R909A (4R->4A) completely abolished all methylation of H3K4.
source: As expected, the quadruple mutant R901A, R904A, R908A and R909A (4R->4A) completely abolished all methylation of H3K4.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Charge reversal mutants Set1 R901E, R904E, R908E, R909E and the quadruple 4R->4E mutants all abolished H3K4 methylation, except for R909E, which retained some residual H3K4 mono-methylation.
source: Charge reversal mutants R901E, R904E, R908E, R909E and the quadruple 4R->4E mutants all abolished H3K4 methylation, expect for R909E, which retained some residual H3K4 mono-methylation (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4g,h.

claim: Interactions between the RxxxRR helix and the acidic patch are critical for COMPASS activity.
source: Together, these structural and mutational data indicate that interactions between the RxxxRR helix and the acidic patch are critical for COMPASS activity.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by mutagenesis data in Figure 4g,h.

claim: The COMPASS-Ubiquitin interaction is different from, and much more extensive than, the interaction between ubiquitin and the MLL1 core complex subunit RbBP5 or Dot1L.
source: The COMPASS-Ubiquitin interaction is different from, and much more extensive than, the interaction between ubiquitin and the MLL1 core complex subunit RbBP5 (Xue et al., 2019) or Dot1L (Anderson et al., 2019; Valencia-Sánchez et al., 2019; Worden et al., 2019), the histone H3K79 methyltransferase which is also stimulated by H2B-Ub (Briggs et al., 2002; McGinty et al., 2008; Ng et al., 2002) (Figure 5a–c).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 5a-c.

claim: The H2B-linked ubiquitin is positioned in different orientations relative to the face of the nucleosome in COMPASS, MLL1, and Dot1L complexes.
source: Moreover, the H2B-linked ubiquitin is positioned in different orientations relative to the face of the nucleosome in each of these complexes (Figure 5d), indicating that H2B-Ub is a conformationally plastic epitope that can be recognized in structurally distinct ways.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Ubiquitin binds to COMPASS in a large cleft located between Swd1, Set1 and Bre2, burying 930 Å2 of total surface area.
source: Ubiquitin binds to COMPASS in a large cleft located between Swd1, Set1 and Bre2 (Figure 6a), burying 930 Å2 of total surface area.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The H2B-linked ubiquitin sits on top of the Set1 RxxxRR helix and makes multiple contacts with the N-terminal and C-terminal extensions of Swd1.
source: The H2B-linked ubiquitin sits on top of the Set1 RxxxRR helix and makes multiple contacts with the N-terminal and C-terminal extensions of Swd1 (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6a,b.

claim: There is substantial connecting density between Bre2 and the N-terminus of ubiquitin that likely corresponds to a 38 amino acid loop in Bre2 (residues 140–178).
source: In addition to the Set1 and Swd1 contacts, there is substantial connecting density between Bre2 and the N-terminus of ubiquitin that likely corresponds to a 38 amino acid loop in Bre2 (residues 140–178) that is unmodeled in our structure (Figure 6a).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The Bre2 loop (residues 140–178) is not found in human or other yeast COMPASS complexes and appears to be specific to the S. cerevisiae COMPASS complex.
source: This Bre2 loop is not found in human or other yeast COMPASS complexes and appears to be specific to the S. cerevisiae COMPASS complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The primary contact between ubiquitin and COMPASS is mediated by the N- and C-terminal extensions of Swd1.
source: The primary contact between ubiquitin and COMPASS is mediated by the N- and C-terminal extensions of Swd1 (Figure 6b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The N- and C- terminal extensions of Swd1 change conformation when bound to ubiquitin compared to the nucleosome-free (apo) structure of COMPASS.
source: Compared to the nucleosome-free (apo) structure of COMPASS (Qu et al., 2018), the N- and C- terminal extensions of Swd1 change conformation when bound to ubiquitin (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: The Swd1 extensions present an extended surface of hydrophobic residues which interact with the ubiquitin C-terminal tail and the hydrophobic 'I44 patch' on ubiquitin comprising I44, V70, L8 and H68.
source: These Swd1 extensions present an extended surface of hydrophobic residues which interact with the ubiquitin C-terminal tail and the hydrophobic 'I44 patch' on ubiquitin comprising I44, V70, L8 and H68 (Figures 5a and 6b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 5a and 6b.

claim: The I44 patch is a canonical interaction surface that is contacted by many different ubiquitin binding proteins.
source: The I44 patch is a canonical interaction surface that is contacted by many different ubiquitin binding proteins (Komander and Rape, 2012), and by the related MLL1 complex subunit, Rbbp5 (Xue et al., 2019) (Figure 5b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 5b.

claim: At the center of the I44 patch interaction, Swd1 L12, V401 and P8 contact Ub I44 and Swd1 F9 interacts with Ub L8, V70, H68 and the aliphatic portion of K6.
source: At the center of the I44 patch interaction, Swd1 L12, V401 and P8 contact Ub I44 and Swd1 F9 interacts with Ub L8, V70, H68 and the aliphatic portion of K6 (Figure 6b,e and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6b,e and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The I44 patch contact is flanked by electrostatic interactions between Swd1 E14 and Ub R42 on one side, and between Swd1 E397 and Ub K48 on the other.
source: The I44 patch contact is flanked by electrostatic interactions between Swd1 E14 and Ub R42 on one side, and between Swd1 E397 and Ub K48 on the other (Figure 6b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Set1 contacts the hydrophobic 'I36 patch' of ubiquitin consisting of I36, L71 and L73.
source: In addition to the I44 patch contacts, Set1 contacts the hydrophobic 'I36 patch' of ubiquitin consisting of I36, L71 and L73 (Figure 6b,f) (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 6b,f.

claim: The I36 patch of ubiquitin is also used by the Dot1L methyltransferase.
source: While the I36 patch of ubiquitin is not as widely utilized by ubiquitin-binding proteins, it is also used by the Dot1L methyltransferase (Figure 5c).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5c.

claim: At the end of the RxxxRR helix, Ub L73 contacts Set1 I914 and the aliphatic portion of N917 through van der Waals interactions.
source: At the end of the RxxxRR helix Ub L73 contacts I914 and the aliphatic portion of N917 through van der Waals interactions (Figure 6b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Ubiquitin residues L71 and L73 are critical for ubiquitin-dependent COMPASS activity.
source: The importance of the L73 contact is supported by previous in vitro studies showing that ubiquitin residues, L71 and L73, are critical for ubiquitin- dependent COMPASS activity (Holt et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: Set1 L928 inserts into a small hydrophobic pocket within ubiquitin and likely interacts with ubiquitin I13, I36, T7 and the aliphatic portion of K11.
source: Finally, Set1 L928 inserts into a small hydrophobic pocket within ubiquitin and likely interacts with ubiquitin I13, I36, T7 and the aliphatic portion of K11 (Figure 6f and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6f and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Swd1 L12A mutation completely abolished H3K4 methylation by COMPASS in vivo.
source: As shown in Figure 6g–h, the Swd1 L12A mutation completely abolished H3K4 methylation by COMPASS in vivo, indicating that the interaction between this Swd1 residue and Ub I44 is critical to COMPASS function.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6g-h.

claim: Swd1 E14A and E14R mutations both greatly decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation and also reduced H3K4 mono-methylation to an intermediate level.
source: Swd1 E14A and E14R mutations both greatly decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation and also reduced H3K4 mono-methylation to an intermediate level (Figure 6g,h).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6g,h.

claim: A Swd1 F9A, L12A and E14A triple mutant (FLE) completely abolished H3K4 methylation.
source: Unsurprisingly, a Swd1 F9A, L12A and E14A triple mutant (FLE) completely abolished H3K4 methylation.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The Swd1 E397R mutation modestly reduced all methylation states of H3K4.
source: Finally, the E397R mutation, which lies on the periphery of the ubiquitin interaction, modestly reduced all methylation states of H3K4 (Figure 6g,h).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6g,h.

claim: The contacts observed between COMPASS and the H2B-linked ubiquitin are critical to activate COMPASS for H3K4 methylation.
source: Together, these data show that the contacts observed between COMPASS and the H2B-linked ubiquitin are critical to activate COMPASS for H3K4 methylation.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and supported by mutagenesis data in Figure 6g,h.

claim: COMPASS methylates its target lysine in an asymmetric manner by recognizing the H2B-Ub and H3K4 on opposite sides of the nucleosome.
source: Our structure reveals the basis of crosstalk between H2B-ubiquitination and H3K4 methylation by Saccharomyces cerevisiae COMPASS and shows that it methylates its target lysine in an asymmetric manner by recognizing the H2B-Ub and H3K4 on opposite sides of the nucleosome (Figure 1d).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The asymmetric recognition of H2B-Ub and H3K4 by COMPASS is distinct from Dot1L, which methylates H3 on the same, cis-H3, side of the nucleosome.
source: This asymmetric recognition is distinct from the H3K79 methyltransferase, Dot1L, which is also stimulated by H2B-Ub but which methylates H3 on the same, cis-H3, side of the nucleosome (Figure 5c) (Anderson et al., 2019; Valencia-Sánchez et al., 2019; Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The asymmetric recognition of H2B-Ub and H3K4 by COMPASS and COMPASS-related complexes is the first example of trans-nucleosome histone crosstalk.
source: To our knowledge, the asymmetric recognition of H2B-Ub and H3K4 by COMPASS and COMPASS-related complexes (Hsu et al., 2019; Xue et al., 2019) is the first example of trans-nucleosome histone crosstalk.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: 'Repressive' H3K27 tri-methyl and 'active' H3K4 tri-methyl marks can be deposited asymmetrically in the same nucleosome, but on opposite H3 tails.
source: Previous studies have shown that 'repressive' H3K27 tri-methyl and 'active' H3K4 tri-methyl marks can be deposited asymmetrically in the same nucleosome, but on opposite H3 tails (Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: Asymmetric, bivalent modification of H3K27 and H3K4 is believed to be associated with maintaining promoters in a poised state during differentiation.
source: This asymmetric, bivalent modification of H3K27 and H3K4 is believed to be associated with maintaining promoters in a poised state during differentiation.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The structure provides a mechanistic framework to understand how asymmetric nucleosome modifications can be read out and deposited during histone crosstalk.
source: Our structure provides a mechanistic framework to understand how asymmetric nucleosome modifications can be read out and deposited during histone crosstalk.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Ubiquitination is a large, highly complex mark that presents a chemically rich interaction surface to potential binding partners and also decompacts chromatin.
source: Compared with other histone modifications such as methylation and acetylation, ubiquitination is a large, highly complex mark that presents a chemically rich interaction surface to potential binding partners and also decompacts chromatin (Fierz et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: Because ubiquitin is conjugated to the nucleosome through its flexible C-terminus, it can adopt a range of orientations on the nucleosome, enabling even greater complexity in its recognition.
source: In addition, because it is conjugated to the nucleosome through its flexible C-terminus, ubiquitin can adopt a range of orientations on the nucleosome, enabling even greater complexity it its recognition.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The distinct ubiquitin binding modes employed by COMPASS, Dot1L and the MLL1 core complex reveal a striking plasticity in how ubiquitin is able to interact with and activate different histone methyltransferases.
source: The distinct ubiquitin binding modes employed by COMPASS (Hsu et al., 2019) (this study), Dot1L (Anderson et al., 2019; Valencia-Sánchez et al., 2019; Worden et al., 2019) and the MLL1 core complex (Xue et al., 2019) reveal a striking plasticity in how ubiquitin is able to interact with and activate these different histone methyltransferases.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The high complexity of the ubiquitin mark likely enables H2B-Ub to communicate with different enzymatic complexes and template the deposition of 'activating' marks during transcription.
source: The high complexity of the ubiquitin mark likely enables H2B-Ub to communicate with these different enzymatic complexes and template the deposition of 'activating' marks during transcription.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: H2B-Ub may impose a steric barrier to the transcriptional machinery as evidenced by the observation that efficient transcription elongation requires removal of H2B-Ub.
source: Indeed, H2B-Ub may even impose a steric barrier to the transcriptional machinery as evidenced by the observation that efficient transcription elongation requires removal of H2B-Ub (Wyce et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: Compared to the nucleosome-free S. cerevisiae COMPASS structure and the structure of K. lactis COMPASS bound to an H3 peptide and SAM, there are no discernable conformational changes in the Set1 catalytic domain that could explain how H2B-Ub stimulates methylation.
source: Compared to the nucleosome-free Saccharomyces cerevisiae COMPASS structure (Qu et al., 2018) and the structure of Kluyveromyces lactis COMPASS bound to an H3 peptide and SAM (Hsu et al., 2018), there are no discernable conformational changes in the Set1 catalytic domain that could explain how H2B-Ub stimulates methylation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: For both COMPASS and Dot1L, the presence of ubiquitin conjugated to H2B does not appear to increase affinity of the enzyme for the nucleosome.
source: It is notable that, for both COMPASS and Dot1L, the presence of ubiquitin conjugated to H2B does not appear to increase affinity of the enzyme for the nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ubiquitin binding primarily affects catalytic activation and, in the case of Dot1L, has been shown to increase kcat but not KM.
source: The lack of a discernable effect on binding energy suggests that ubiquitin binding primarily affects catalytic activation and, in the case of Dot1L, has been shown to increase kcat but not KM (McGinty et al., 2009; Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Ubiquitin activates Dot1L by using its binding energy to pay the energetic cost of inducing a conformational change in the globular core of histone H3, thereby inserting K79 into the Dot1L active site.
source: Alternatively, It has been suggested that ubiquitin activates Dot1L by using its binding energy to pay the energetic cost of inducing a conformational change in the globular core of histone H3, thereby inserting K79 into the Dot1L active site (Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: H2B-Ub may activate COMPASS by providing the binding energy needed to induce the disordered Set1 RxxxRR motif to form a helix that mediates contacts with the nucleosome.
source: We speculate that H2B-Ub may similarly activate COMPASS by providing the binding energy needed to induce the disordered Set1 RxxxRR motif to form a helix that mediates contacts with the nucleosome.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Ubiquitin binding may compensate for the energetic cost of inducing the Set1 helix, 326–331, to unravel and form an extended β-strand that buttresses the RxxxRR helix and the catalytic domain of Set1.
source: Ubiquitin binding may also compensate for the energetic cost of inducing the Set1 helix, 326–331, to unravel and form an extended β-strand that buttresses the RxxxRR helix and the catalytic domain of Set1 (Figure 4).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The structure provides a basis for further elucidating the role that H2B ubiquitination plays in stimulating histone methyltransferase activity.
source: Our structure provides a basis for further elucidating the role that H2B ubiquitination plays in stimulating histone methyltransferase activity.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The ubiquitinated nucleosome was prepared using a Xenopus laevis nucleosome core particle ubiquitinated at histone H2B K120 via a non-hydrolyzable dichloroacetone (DCA) linkage.
source: We determined the cryo-EM structure of the minimal, H2B-ubiquitin-sensing subcomplex of Saccharomyces cerevisiae COMPASS bound to a Xenopus laevis nucleosome core particle ubiquitinated at histone H2B K120 via a non-hydrolyzable dichloroacetone (DCA) linkage (Morgan et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: The ubiquitinated residue H2B K120 in Xenopus laevis corresponds to K123 of yeast H2B.
source: The ubiquitinated residue corresponds to K123 of yeast H2B.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: A variant of histone H3 in which K4 was substituted with norleucine (Nle) was used to drive tight association between COMPASS and the nucleosome.
source: To drive tight association between COMPASS and the nucleosome, we utilized a variant of histone H3 in which K4 was substituted with the non-native amino acid, norleucine (Nle) (Worden et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: The final COMPASS-nucleosome structure was determined to 3.37 Å resolution.
source: We therefore prepared complexes between COMPASS and H2B-Ub nucleosomes containing the H3K4Nle mutation in the presence of saturating SAM and determined the structure of the complex to 3.37 Å by single particle cryo-EM (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplements 2–3 and Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Table 1.

claim: The final model includes one COMPASS complex and the nucleosome core particle.
source: The final model, therefore, includes one COMPASS complex and the nucleosome core particle (Figure 1a–b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1a-b.

claim: Models of Spp1 and the N-set region of Set1 were taken from the cryo-EM structure of S. cerevisiae COMPASS.
source: To build the yeast COMPASS complex, models of Spp1 and the N-set region of Set1 were taken from the cryo-EM structure of S. cerevisiae COMPASS (Qu et al., 2018) and docked into the EM density.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: Crystal structures of K. lactis Bre2, Swd1, Swd3, Sdc1 and Set1 subunits were utilized to create homology models with the S. cerevisiae sequence.
source: For the rest of the COMPASS model, crystal structures of K. lactis Bre2, Swd1, Swd3, Sdc1 and Set1 subunits (Hsu et al., 2018) were utilized to create homology models with the S. cerevisiae sequence (25%–50% sequence identity) using Swiss-model (Waterhouse et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Spp1, Bre2 and the Sdc1 dimer are less well resolved than the other COMPASS subunits due to their location on the periphery of the complex and consequent higher mobility.
source: Spp1, Bre2 and the Sdc1 dimer are less well resolved than the other COMPASS subunits due to their location on the periphery of the complex and consequent higher mobility (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The EM density corresponding to the N-terminal portion of Spp1 was very weak and precluded accurate model fitting.
source: In particular, the EM density corresponding to the N-terminal portion of Spp1 was very weak and precluded accurate model fitting.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The N-terminal portion of Spp1 was excluded from the final model.
source: Therefore, the N-terminal portion of Spp1 was excluded from our final model (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: COMPASS flexing allows Spp1 to bind the nucleosomal DNA and allows Swd1 to interact with the histone core.
source: This movement allows Spp1 to bind the nucleosomal DNA, and allows Swd1 to interact with the histone core.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: A subset of particles in the cryo-EM structure of COMPASS in the absence of nucleosome exhibited flexing about the same axis, although not to the extent observed when COMPASS is bound to a nucleosome.
source: Notably, a subset of particles in the cryo-EM structure of COMPASS in the absence of nucleosome (Qu et al., 2018) exhibited flexing about the same axis, although not to the extent observed here when COMPASS is bound to a nucleosome (Figure 1c).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation and shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The previously observed conformational flexibility of COMPASS is important for nucleosome recognition.
source: Our structure suggests that the previously observed conformational flexibility of COMPASS is important for nucleosome recognition.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The 88 Å end-to-end distance between the exit point of cis-H3 and H3 in the Set1 active site is too long to be spanned by the intervening unstructured H3 tail residues.
source: The 88 Å end-to-end distance between the exit point of cis-H3 and H3 in the Set1 active site is too long to be spanned by the intervening unstructured H3 tail residues given that an even greater distance (~100 Å) would be needed for the H3 residues to wrap around the nucleosomal DNA near the dyad axis.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Swd1 V263 and I264 are in van der Waals contact with H2A Y50 and H2B V118.
source: This hydrophobic crevice includes H2A Y50, and H2B V118, which are in van der Waals contact with Swd1 V263 and I264.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Swd1 N265 is positioned close to H2B Q95, potentially forming a hydrogen bond.
source: In addition to the hydrophobic interactions in L, Swd1 N265 is positioned close to H2B Q95, potentially forming a hydrogen bond and further stabilizing the Loop 1 interaction with the histone core (Figure 3b).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The Swd1 V263A mutant slightly decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation, but did not change H3K4 mono-methylation.
source: The V263A mutant slightly decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation, but did not change H3K4 mono-methylation, whereas an N265A mutation had no effect (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3c,d.

claim: The Swd1 N265A mutation had no effect on H3K4 methylation.
source: The V263A mutant slightly decreased H3K4 di- and tri-methylation, but did not change H3K4 mono-methylation, whereas an N265A mutation had no effect (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3c,d.

claim: This concave DNA binding surface is lined with several basic residues that can potentially contact the DNA.
source: This concave surface is lined with several basic residues that can potentially contact the DNA.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Set1 residues R1034, K1029 and K1026 are located at the Bre2-Set1 DNA binding interface but are too far away to directly contact the DNA.
source: Set1 residues R1034, K1029 and K1026 are also located at this interface (Figure 2b) but are too far away to directly contact the DNA.
evidence: Stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Set1 basic residues R1034, K1029 and K1026 likely serve to increase the local positive charge of the concave DNA binding surface.
source: Instead, these basic residues likely serve to increase the local positive charge of the concave DNA binding surface.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: Fragmented density connecting Spp1 and the nucleosomal DNA corresponds to a loop in Spp1 that is disordered in the structure (residues 241–261).
source: Fragmented density connecting Spp1 and the nucleosomal DNA corresponds to a loop in Spp1 that is disordered in our structure (residues 241–261).
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The conformational change in Set1 helix 926–933 alleviates what would otherwise be steric clash between the N-terminus of the helix formed by these residues in uncomplexed (Apo) COMPASS.
source: The conformational change in this region of Set1 alleviates what would otherwise be steric clash between the N-terminus of the helix formed by these residues in uncomplexed (Apo) COMPASS.
evidence: Stated in the Results section.

claim: The N- and C-terminal extensions of Swd1 are critical for COMPASS assembly and mediate multiple contacts between COMPASS subunits.
source: These Swd1 extensions are critical for COMPASS assembly and mediate multiple contacts between COMPASS subunits (Hsu et al., 2018; Qu et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: H3K4 methylation can serve as a recruitment signal for various transcription activators.
source: H3K4 methylation can serve as a recruitment signal for various transcription activators (Sims et al., 2007; Vermeulen et al., 2010; Vermeulen et al., 2007; Wysocka et al., 2006) including SAGA, whose acetyltransferase activity is stimulated by H3K4 methylation (Bian et al., 2011; Ringel et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SAGA acetyltransferase activity is stimulated by H3K4 methylation.
source: H3K4 methylation can serve as a recruitment signal for various transcription activators (Sims et al., 2007; Vermeulen et al., 2010; Vermeulen et al., 2007; Wysocka et al., 2006) including SAGA, whose acetyltransferase activity is stimulated by H3K4 methylation (Bian et al., 2011; Ringel et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Set1 can attach up to three methyl groups to the H3K4 lysine ε-amino group.
source: H3K4 is methylated in yeast by the Set1 methyltransferase (Roguev et al., 2001), which can attach up to three methyl groups to the lysine ε-amino group (Santos-Rosa et al., 2002)
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: H2B-ubiquitination and H3K4 methylation is an example of histone modification 'cross-talk' in which attachment of one histone mark templates the deposition of another.
source: Methylation of nucleosomal H3K4 depends on the prior ubiquitination of histone H2B (H2B-Ub) at Lysine 120 (Lys 123 in yeast) (Dover et al., 2002; Shahbazian et al., 2005; Sun and Allis, 2002), an example of histone modification 'cross-talk' in which attachment of one histone mark templates the deposition of another.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.
